question.leadin: After this battle, Pheidippides ran approximately 26 miles to Athens to announce a Greek victory.
question.text: Name this 490 BCE battle that lends its name to a very long race.
question.clue: Datis and Artaphernes were stopped from moving inland by the presence of troops positioned in a swamp, led by Miltiades.

swap.leadin: The Phaistos Disc, an artifact found in one of this civilization's palaces, may represent an undeciphered writing system.
swap.text: Name this ancient civilization from the island of Crete, which also developed the Linear A writing system.
swap.clue: A devastating blow this civilization occurred when the Thera volcano erupted in the 16th century BCE, which contributed to their eventual decline and the occupation by the Mycenaean Greeks.

question.leadin: -- give the following about classical historians.
question.text: This Athenian general included Pericles' funeral oration in book two of his History of the Peloponnesian War.
question.clue: This man included the Melian Dialogue in his major work, which also contains a notoriously difficult-to-translate Funeral Oration.

swap.leadin: The introduction of the sarissa pike by this country's Philip II revolutionized its military.
swap.text: Name this ancient country that gained control of Greece after winning at Chaeronea. A modern country of this name has capital at Skopje.
swap.answerHtml: Macedonia [accept Macedon, prompt “Former Yugoslav Republic of Macedonia” or “Fyrom” ]
swap.clue: In 1995, this country was forced to remove a 16-rayed sun from its flag, as part of a dispute that still keeps it out of the EU.

question.text: Multiple members of the Annales school, wrote their theses about this Spanish king's influence on politics in the Mediterranean. He sent the warships that won the Battle of Lepanto.
question.answerHtml: Philip II [“the second”] [accept Felipe II; prompt on Philip and Felipe]
question.clue: The Relaciones of this king's disgraced secretary Antonio Perez contributed to the "Black Legend" of this king, who as a prince received an early copy of Bartolome de las Casas's A Short Account of the Destruction of the Indies.

swap.leadin: The first half of this war ended with the signing of the Peace of Nicias.
swap.text: Name this 5th century BCE war, fought for almost thirty years, between Athens and Sparta.
swap.clue: The traitor Alcibiades led the ill-fated Sicilian Expedition for one side in this war that ultimately lost at the 405 BC Battle of Aegospotami.

question.leadin: This ruler died after a Laconic woman dropped a tile on his head during a Siege of Argos.
question.text: Name this ruler who allegedly exclaimed "One more victory and we are undone!" after a victory at the Battle of Asculum. The term for a costly victory is named after this ruler.
question.clue: The Romans renamed the town of Maleventum to Beneventum after this man fought there on behalf of Tarentum.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about the LBA collapse.
swap.text: LBA stands for Late [this age], which came after the Stone Age and before the Iron Age.
swap.clue: Earlier in this time period, Greece had been home to the Minoans.

question.leadin: Answer these questions about ancient writing.
question.text: This precursor to ancient Greek was found on records excavated at Mycenae and deciphered in the 1950s.
question.clue: This system consists of ninety syllabic signs, all of which correspond to open syllables.

swap.leadin: Identify the following about some examples of Ancient Greek humor.
swap.text: This historian collected the pithy sayings of Laconic Women in one book. His best known work begins by comparing Theseus with Romulus.
swap.clue: This author of the Moralia praises Marcellus and Brutus while disapproving of Sulla and Antony, and analyzes the military tactics of Fabius Cunctator and Pericles.

question.text: The only permitted political party under Franco's regime was a fascist party named for this military formation. This rectangular formation of spearmen was made up of hoplites in Ancient Greece.
question.clue: Two successive political parties with this name were merged with the Councils of the National-Syndicalist Offensive and the Carlist Party respectively.

swap.text: The Helot population comprised almost entirely of residents from the south of this peninsula, where the city of Sparta is located. This peninsula's north contains the city of Delphi.
swap.answerHtml: the Peloponnese [or Peloponnesian peninsula or Peloponnesia or Peloponnesus or Morea; prompt on Greek peninsula]
swap.clue: It's not in Algeria, but Jean-Baptiste Bory de Saint-Vincent directed a scientific commission that accompanied an 1828 military expedition to this region.

question.text: According to Strabo, slave trading became rife on this island after the Romans captured it from Perseus of Macedon and made it a free port. Athenian executions would not take place until a sacred ship returned to this island.
question.clue: Dying in this location was prohibited in a ritual purification during the Peloponnesian War.

swap.leadin: This man legendarily promulgated an oral constitution that established the Gerousia, a council of 28 elders.
swap.text: Name this lawgiver whose Rhetra also included a dual monarchy for Sparta.
swap.clue: This legendary lawgiver who established the Great Rhetra constitution, outlined the function of the five ephors, and called for a council of twenty-eight men known as the gerousia to wield equal power to the two royal houses.

question.text: The non-royal commander of the Spartan fleet which finally defeated the Athenians at the Battle of Notium and paved the way for the final defeat of Athens in the Peloponnesian War, he later came to dominate Spartan politics.
question.clue: This beneficiary of Cyrus the Younger's patronage resumed his most famous office after his replacement Callicratidas lost the battle of Arginusae.

swap.leadin: All male citizens were mandated to perform this program except for the firstborn sons of the Eurypontid and Agiad houses.
swap.text: Name this rigorous education and military training program employed by Sparta that included the paides, paidiskoi, and hebontes stages for boys starting at the age of 7 until they turned 29.
swap.clue: Following completion of this system, its participants joined in the krypteia to control the population of helots.

question.leadin: The final city usually included in this group became the site of the Italiote League, which was eventually destroyed at the Battle of the Elleporus.
question.text: Give this term which refers to a group of colonies along the coast of southern Italy, starting with the Euboean colonies of Cumae and Pithecusae around 750 BC and ending with Heraclea circa 433 BC.
question.clue: Tarquin the Proud died in exile in a city in this region.

swap.leadin: Answer some questions about Thrasybulus, the arch-democrat who repeatedly thwarted Athenian oligarchic regimes such as the short-lived 400 and the more durable and brutal Thirty Tyrants.
swap.text: Thrasybulus prevented the 400's takeover of this island, led in a namesake war against Athens by the philosopher Melissus. Polycrates had The Tunnel of Eupalinos, an advanced underground aqueduct, built on it.
swap.clue: Herodotus claims that the pharaoh Ahmose broke off Egypt's alliance with this city-state after its tyrant discovered his lost ring in the belly of a fish.

question.leadin: The terms on which Sicily became a Roman province obliged Rome to abide by the Law of Hiero and tax tenant farmers no more than 1/10th the value of their output.
question.text: Hiero was a tyrant of this city, which had been an ally of Rome's in the first Punic War. This city joined the Carthaginians in the second war and the city was sacked, though not before the quasi-mythical burning of Roman ships with an enormous death ray.
question.clue: The Spartan general Gyllipus defended this city from Athenians under Nicias during an expedition in the Peloponnesian War, and it was originally a Corinthian colony.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about difficult scripts from around the world.
swap.text: This object recovered from a Minoan palace in 1908 by Luigi Pernier contains an undeciphered script spiralled along both sides. The language on this object is neither Linear A nor Linear B.
